label: MEASURED
purpose: BBC (bbc.exe after XAX ledger 0022: constant folding on x86-64) against the same eight pinned competitors, same 18 programs (sources by hash), on one Linux host; same runner as 2026-11-07

method.runner: compete.py and peakrss.c outside both repositories (sha256 in runner_sha256, peakrss_sha256); analyze.py for the summaries
method.trials: one validation build and run per arm (also the warmup), then 5 build and 5 run trials, interleaved across arms with the order rotated each trial; medians per program, geometric means per group
method.timing: wall time fork..wait of one fresh process tree under a static launcher; peak RSS from RUSAGE_CHILDREN (launcher floor about 1.6 MiB)
method.correctness: stdout bytes and exit 0 equal brainfry bfinterp's on the same input; a mismatching arm is not timed for that program
method.platforms: BBC (-O1, -O0) and brainfry-win build Windows x86-64 executables and run under Wine 9.0 (persistent wineserver; about a 30 ms process floor); the others build and run natively on Linux x86-64. Compare Windows rows with Windows rows.
method.inputs: the 2026-10-22 inputs where recoverable (from wide_reset_evidence.json); factor (133333333333) and life (a glider, 20 generations, q) are new because the old inputs are recorded only as hashes

findings: No competitor is beaten under the rulebook (docs/06): build time still fails every pairing but Brainfly, and Brainfly's run time and the Wine floor fail that one.

Same platform (both under Wine): BBC O1's run time is 1.069x brainfry-win's over 17 programs (the Wine process floor dominates the small ones). mandelbrot is now faster: 1147 vs 1250 ms; factor 60.6 vs 53.1 ms and life 46.5 vs 35.0 ms are still slower.

Against the 2026-11-07 run on the same host: BBC O1 mandelbrot 1147 ms (was 1,635), factor 60.6 (was 78.6), life 46.5 (was 62.1); executables 7% smaller against every competitor. The host ran faster this day (brainfry-win's mandelbrot 1,250 vs 1,466 ms), so compare arms within one run.
pablojorge's nested_math mismatch is unchanged (its tape is not zero-initialized).
All BBC runs are under Wine on Linux: not Windows-native or device runs (BLOCKED for the rulebook's device sweep).
